headline: COPPER GIANT IN WAITING: Anglo-Teck $54B Merger One Chinese Stamp Away — 11-Day Countdown Set
snippet: Teck Resources and Anglo American have locked in a final 11-trading-day countdown window to close their proposed $54 billion all-stock merger of equals — meaning the deal can execute rapidly once the last regulatory approvals land. China and South Korea remain the only outstanding antitrust jurisdictions, with the closing window originally set between September 2026 and March 2027. The combined Anglo Teck, headquartered in Vancouver, would produce roughly 1.2 million tonnes of copper annually, making it one of the world's largest copper miners and a dominant force at a time when copper supply is increasingly constrained.

headline: CHINA NUCLEAR BANKROLLS NAMIBIA: Bannerman's $321.5M CNNC JV Clears All Conditions, FID Targeted Q4 2026
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) confirmed on September 9 that CNNC Overseas Limited — a subsidiary of China National Nuclear Corp — satisfied all conditions precedent to its US$321.5 million strategic investment for a 45% stake in an Etango joint venture, unlocking a final investment decision targeted for Q4 2026. To complete project financing, Bannerman simultaneously launched an A$124 million fully underwritten equity placement. The Etango mine in Namibia's Erongo Region would produce approximately 3.5 million pounds of uranium per year; CNNC retains 60% life-of-mine offtake. Deep Yellow (ASX: DYL) is also advancing its nearby Tumas uranium project toward a year-end FID, presenting its strategy to utilities at the World Nuclear Association Symposium in London this week.

headline: CHILE COPPER WALL: Marimaca Drills 216m of 0.96% Cu — 62m Core Hits 2.2% Cu and 21.5 g/t Ag
snippet: Marimaca Copper (TSX: MARI; ASX: MC2) reported hole SPRD-15 at its Pampa Medina deposit in Chile's Antofagasta Region cut 216 metres grading 0.96% copper and 7.2 g/t silver from 466 metres depth, including a high-grade 62-metre interval at 2.2% copper and 21.5 g/t silver from 602 metres. Step-out drilling extended the copper-silver system 300 metres beyond earlier holes, with Pampa Medina sitting 28 km east of Marimaca's more advanced oxide deposit. Shares rose 12.98% to a TSX top-gainer position on the news, with the 2026 program now focused on delineating the high-grade core and further step-outs.

headline: NEW ZEALAND'S GOLD-ANTIMONY MOTHERLODE: RUA GOLD Drills 82.9 g/t Au + 24.8% Sb in Single Interval
snippet: RUA Gold (CSE: RUA) posted its highest-grade results ever at the Auld Creek Gold-Antimony Project in Reefton, New Zealand: a standout 0.6-metre interval at 136.2 g/t gold equivalent — comprising 82.9 g/t gold and 24.8% antimony — alongside broader hits of 7.0 metres at 9.9 g/t AuEq and 32.0 metres at 2.4 g/t AuEq, plus the first observation of visible gold. With 19,600 metres of 2026 drilling complete, a pre-feasibility study is on track for Q4 2026, and the New Zealand government has formally recognized Auld Creek under the Fast-Track Approvals Act — replacing a fragmented multi-statute process with a single six-month expert panel review. China's antimony export restrictions make any high-grade Western antimony source strategically significant.

headline: GOLD'S 2026 GAINS ERASED: Metal Now Up Just 0.7% Year-to-Date, Sitting 20% Below $5,419 January Record
snippet: After gold's stunning 33% rally for gold mining stocks in August — the best August for the NYSE Arca Gold Miners Index since at least 1994 — September's combination of a 5.4% PPI print and a hotter-than-expected core CPI has wiped out gold's full-year gains, leaving bullion up just 0.7% for 2026 and about 20% below its January 28 record close of $5,419.83. Fed rate-hike odds have now reached 90% on the CME FedWatch tool following today's August CPI. Silver remains up 59% over 12 months despite the September reversal, underscoring how different the two metals' fundamentals are even as their short-term moves are correlated.

headline: THE MAKE-OR-BREAK WEEK: What September 15-16 Fed Decision Means for Gold and Silver Investors
snippet: With September 15-16 FOMC meeting now the defining near-term event for precious metals, GoldSilver.com maps out the bull and bear scenarios: a rate hike (now priced at 90% odds) could push gold toward the $4,050–$4,100 support zone, while a hold or dovish surprise could fuel a snap-back toward the $4,720–$4,830 major resistance. Critically, futures positioning is crowded long with roughly 228,000 net managed-money contracts heading into a binary event — an unusual setup that raises the odds of an outsized move in either direction. The piece argues that whatever the near-term outcome, the long-term case rooted in central-bank demand, debt dynamics, and geopolitical hedging remains structurally intact.

headline: CONVICTION BUY: Sprott Uranium Report — Miners +17% in September, WNA Forecasts Reactor Demand Doubles by 2040
snippet: Sprott's September uranium report documents a sharp reversal: spot uranium rebounded to US$82 per pound (+8.05% month-to-date), the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index climbed 17.01%, and junior uranium miners gained 21.75% — outpacing gold equities and broader commodities. Supply risks deepened as Cameco cut McArthur River production guidance and Kazatomprom reduced 2026 targets, compounding a structural deficit now reinforced by the World Nuclear Association's latest demand forecast that projects reactor requirements to more than double by 2040, boosted by small modular reactors and data-centre power purchase agreements from major technology companies.

headline: EUROPE KILLS CHINA BATTERY LOOP: EU Classifies Black Mass Hazardous, Bans Exports to Non-OECD From November
snippet: The European Union has classified black mass — the material recovered from shredded end-of-life lithium-ion batteries — as hazardous waste, and the measure becomes mandatory across all member states on November 9, 2026, with some countries already enforcing it. Under the Basel Ban Amendment, this classification prohibits EU nations from shipping black mass to non-OECD countries, effectively ending the flow of European battery recycling feedstock to Chinese processors who had been reclassifying the same material as non-waste. The move is expected to accelerate European domestic battery recycling capacity, raise costs for Chinese cathode makers, and strengthen the economics of North American and European battery materials developers.

headline: LIGHT RARE EARTHS IN FREEFALL: Cerium Crashes 13.8% in August, Chinese Oversupply Overwhelms Green Demand
snippet: While geopolitical attention has focused on Beijing's export controls on heavy rare earths, a different crisis is unfolding in light rare earths: cerium fell 13.8% in August and a further 5.83% in September to US$3.88 per kilogram, with no visible demand catalyst to absorb the structural oversupply flowing from Chinese and expanding Western light rare earth production. The September outlook report notes that expanding Western rare earth projects — designed to reduce Chinese dependence — are paradoxically entering a market where Chinese producers continue to set the price floor, raising difficult questions about project viability for light-REE-heavy developers targeting neodymium-praseodymium oxide as their sole revenue driver.

headline: BANKS HOLD TARGETS: HSBC $4,560 Average, JPMorgan Q4 $4,500 — September Selloff Seen As Re-Entry Window
snippet: Major institutional forecasters have not materially revised their gold outlook despite September's sharp reversal, maintaining that the pullback represents a tactical re-entry opportunity rather than a structural trend change. HSBC forecasts a 2026 annual average of US$4,560 with a year-end marker of $4,750, while JPMorgan targets a Q4 average near $4,500 — both sitting comfortably above gold's current $4,380 level. The September update also consolidates HSBC's silver forecast of $75 per ounce average for 2026, representing a 17% upside from spot, though analysts caution that the Fed's September decision could temporarily breach support before the recovery phase.
